public_rationale: Zitron presents this as his own view ('I posit') about how much people understand GPU prices and data-center economics. 'Little understanding' has no threshold, and he does not say whose understanding he means. There is no standard measure of collective understanding, so the claim cannot be scored true or false. Silicon Data's H100 index page, updated 2026-10-28, publishes daily hourly rental readings. The page says the readings come from neo-cloud providers and GPU marketplaces, with hyperscaler prices published separately. It says every input is adjusted for rental term length, cluster scale, and interconnect (e1). The page does not report realized long-term contract prices. A May 2025 IEEE Spectrum article titled 'Price Index Could Clarify Opaque GPU Costs for AI' described GPU costs as opaque (e2). These items are relevant to the debate, but they cannot show whether understanding is 'little'.
limitations: No item reports realized long-term GPU contract prices or data-center unit economics.
The IEEE Spectrum item (e2) is a single article from May 2025. It does not describe public knowledge in October 2026 or show how widely the opacity concern is held.
The Silicon Data page (e1) is the company's own description of its product.
Side points, such as whether the index favors spot pricing, are not the claim itself, and e1 does not settle them.

statement.excerpt: I posit that we have little understanding of the true price that people are paying for AI GPUs, or about the underlying economics of AI data centers writ large.

from_speaker: the true price that people are paying for AI GPUs
the underlying economics of AI data centers writ large
our_interpretation: This is a framed opinion ('I posit') about how much the public and investors collectively know. It is not a statement about a number.
'Little understanding' has no threshold. There is no ordinary measure of how much knowledge would count as more than 'little'.
The claim describes an ongoing state. If it were scored, the period would be the state of public knowledge around the post date (October 2026).
criteria.support_condition: Would be supported if public sources showed that realized long-term GPU contract prices and data-center operating economics are mostly undisclosed, and that the public price benchmarks disagree with each other or reflect mainly short-term rentals.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted if realized contract prices and data-center unit economics were widely and consistently disclosed, for example in filings and in benchmarks that agree with each other.
